title: The symmetric monoidal structure on $\mathcal A$-valued sheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ and $C$ be as in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf]; for instance $C$ is the
small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ of a scheme ([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]) or the
category of profinite sets with the coherent topology, and $\mathcal A=\Ab$ with
$\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ and unit $\mathbf Z$, or $\mathcal A=\Mod_R$ for a commutative ring $R$.
For sheaves $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ define:

- the *tensor product* $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G:=a(\mathcal F\otimes_p\mathcal G)$, with
  $a$ sheafification, and on morphisms $a(\varphi\otimes_p\psi)$;
- the *unit* $\mathbf 1_{\Sh}:=a(\underline{\mathbf 1})$;
- the *associator*
  $(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G)\otimes\mathcal H\cong\mathcal F\otimes(\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal H)$
  as the composite
  $$
  a\bigl(a(\mathcal F\otimes_p\mathcal G)\otimes_p\mathcal H\bigr)\cong a\bigl((\mathcal F\otimes_p\mathcal G)\otimes_p\mathcal H\bigr)\xrightarrow{a(\alpha)}a\bigl(\mathcal F\otimes_p(\mathcal G\otimes_p\mathcal H)\bigr)\cong a\bigl(\mathcal F\otimes_pa(\mathcal G\otimes_p\mathcal H)\bigr),
  $$
  where $\alpha$ is the objectwise associator and the outer isomorphisms are $a$ applied to the
  maps $\eta\otimes_p\mathcal H$, $\mathcal F\otimes_p\eta$ (units of $a$), which are invertible
  after $a$ by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso];
- the *unitors* and the *symmetry* in the same way from the objectwise ones and the unit maps
  $\underline{\mathbf 1}\to a(\underline{\mathbf 1})$.

Then $(\Sh(C,\mathcal A),\otimes,\mathbf 1_{\Sh})$ is a symmetric monoidal category, and
sheafification $a\colon(\mathrm{PSh}(C,\mathcal A),\otimes_p)\to(\Sh(C,\mathcal A),\otimes)$ is
strong symmetric monoidal, with structure isomorphisms
$a(F)\otimes a(G)=a(aF\otimes_paG)\cong a(F\otimes_pG)$ and
$\mathbf 1_{\Sh}=a(\underline{\mathbf 1})$. For $\mathcal A=\Ab$, $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G$ is the
sheafified objectwise $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ and the unit is the constant sheaf
$\underline{\mathbf Z}$.

proof.text:
For a finite family of presheaves $F_1,\dots,F_n$, every iterated sheaf tensor product of the
$aF_\nu$ (any bracketing, with units inserted) receives a canonical map from the iterated
objectwise tensor product of the $F_\nu$ with the same bracketing, built from units of $a$; by
[det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso] (applied repeatedly, using 2 for the inner factors) it
becomes an isomorphism after sheafification. Call these the *canonical isomorphisms*
$a(F_1\otimes_p\dots\otimes_pF_n)\cong aF_1\otimes\dots\otimes aF_n$.

By construction, each structure map of $\Sh(C,\mathcal A)$ (associator, unitors, symmetry) is
the conjugate of $a$ of the corresponding objectwise structure map by canonical isomorphisms.
Every composite of structure maps occurring in the pentagon, triangle and hexagon identities is
therefore the conjugate of $a$ of the corresponding composite of objectwise structure maps, by
the canonical isomorphisms at its two ends; the intermediate canonical isomorphisms cancel
because they are all induced by units of $a$, and the units are natural. Since the identities
hold objectwise ([det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf]), they hold for sheaves. Similarly
$\beta_{\mathcal G,\mathcal F}\circ\beta_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}=\mathrm{id}$ because it holds
objectwise. Naturality of all structure maps follows from naturality of the units.

The structure isomorphisms of $a$ are the canonical isomorphisms for $n=2$ and $n=0$. The
compatibility of $a$ with associators, unitors and symmetries is again the statement that the
sheaf structure maps are conjugates of $a$ of the presheaf ones by canonical isomorphisms, which
holds by definition. So $a$ is strong symmetric monoidal.

For $\mathcal A=\Ab$, the definitions specialize to the sheafified objectwise
$\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$, and $a(\underline{\mathbf Z})$ is by definition the constant sheaf
$\underline{\mathbf Z}$.
